database_summary: Small clinical dataset with three tables: Patient (demographic/descriptive entity at patient level), Examination (clinical exam events/measurements per patient with antibody/lab-related fields and diagnosis flags), and Laboratory (laboratory measurement events per patient and date). Patient holds mostly stable descriptive attributes. Examination and Laboratory are event/measurement tables keyed by patient (and for Laboratory also by Date). Several boolean/text coded flags use small enumerations. Foreign keys: Examination.ID -> Patient.ID, Laboratory.ID -> Patient.ID.

accepted.name: patient_core
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  SEX,
  Birthday,
  "Description",
  "First Date",
  Admission,
  Diagnosis
FROM
  Patient
accepted.description: One-row-per-patient demographic projection exposing key patient identifiers and stable attributes. Use as the base patient cohort for joins, filters, and demographic grouping. | Use for: List patients with demographics; Join patients to their latest lab or exam; Aggregate patients by SEX or Admission status

accepted.name: examination_events
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  "Examination Date",
  "aCL IgG",
  "aCL IgM",
  ANA,
  "ANA Pattern",
  "aCL IgA",
  Diagnosis,
  KCT,
  RVVT,
  LAC,
  Symptoms,
  Thrombosis
FROM
  Examination
accepted.description: Event-level projection of Examination rows (one per examination event) exposing date, serology measures, flags and diagnosis. Use for time-windowed analyses, counts of exams, or joining to labs on date. | Use for: Count examinations per patient or time period; Find exams with positive antibody measures or thrombosis events; Join examinations to laboratory measurements on same or nearest date

accepted.name: latest_laboratory_per_patient_ranked
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  Date,
  GOT,
  GPT,
  LDH,
  ALP,
  TP,
  ALB,
  UA,
  UN,
  CRE,
  "T-BIL",
  "T-CHO",
  TG,
  CPK,
  GLU,
  WBC,
  RBC,
  HGB,
  HCT,
  PLT,
  PT,
  APTT,
  FG,
  PIC,
  TAT,
  TAT2,
  "U-PRO",
  IGG,
  IGA,
  IGM,
  CRP,
  RA,
  RF,
  C3,
  C4,
  RNP,
  SM,
  SC170,
  SSA,
  SSB,
  CENTROMEA,
  DNA,
  "DNA-II",
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ID ORDER BY Date DESC) AS row_number_rank
FROM
  Laboratory
accepted.description: One-row-per-laboratory-event with a descending date rank per patient. Exposes row_number_rank so downstream queries can pick the latest (WHERE row_number_rank = 1) or top-N lab events per patient. | Use for: Select the most recent laboratory record per patient; Return the N most recent lab events per patient (WHERE row_number_rank <= N)

accepted.name: examination_counts_per_patient
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  COUNT(*) AS total_exams,
  MIN("Examination Date") AS first_exam_date,
  MAX("Examination Date") AS last_exam_date,
  SUM(CASE WHEN Thrombosis IS NOT NULL AND Thrombosis != 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_thrombosis_events
FROM
  Examination
GROUP BY
  ID
accepted.description: Per-patient aggregated counts and simple summaries of Examination events: total_exams, first_exam_date, last_exam_date, and count_thrombosis_events. Useful for cohort selection or per-patient profiling. | Use for: Find patients with multiple examinations; Identify patients with any thrombosis events; Filter patients by recency of exams (using last_exam_date)

accepted.name: laboratory_summary_per_patient
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  MIN(GOT) AS GOT_min,
  MAX(GOT) AS GOT_max,
  AVG(GOT) AS GOT_avg,
  MIN(GPT) AS GPT_min,
  MAX(GPT) AS GPT_max,
  AVG(GPT) AS GPT_avg,
  MIN(CRP) AS CRP_min,
  MAX(CRP) AS CRP_max,
  AVG(CRP) AS CRP_avg,
  MIN(Date) AS first_lab_date,
  MAX(Date) AS last_lab_date
FROM
  Laboratory
GROUP BY
  ID
accepted.description: Per-patient summary statistics for key numeric laboratory measures (min, max, avg, last_date). Includes last_seen_date for each patient to help with recency filtering. | Use for: Compare average lab values across patients or cohorts; Select patients with recent labs (using last_lab_date); Find patients with extreme lab values

accepted.name: patient_with_latest_lab
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.ID,
  p.SEX,
  p.Birthday,
  p."Description",
  p."First Date",
  p.Admission,
  p.Diagnosis,
  l.Date,
  l.GOT,
  l.GPT,
  l.LDH,
  l.ALP,
  l.TP,
  l.ALB,
  l.CRP,
  l."T-CHO",
  l.GLU,
  l.WBC,
  l.RBC,
  l.HGB,
  l.HCT,
  l.PLT
FROM
  patient_core p
  JOIN latest_laboratory_per_patient_ranked l ON p.ID = l.ID
WHERE
  l.row_number_rank = 1
accepted.description: Denormalized view joining patient demographics to their most recent laboratory event. Use to display current patient status or to feed analyses that need one lab-per-patient (latest). Relies on latest_laboratory_per_patient_ranked to identify latest record. | Use for: Show patient demographics alongside their most recent lab; Build a cohort of patients with recent abnormal labs (filter on CRP, GOT, etc.)

accepted.name: exam_lab_same_day_candidates
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.ID AS ID,
  e."Examination Date" AS Examination_Date,
  l.Date AS Laboratory_Date,
  e."aCL IgG" AS "aCL IgG",
  e."aCL IgM" AS "aCL IgM",
  e.ANA AS ANA,
  e."ANA Pattern" AS "ANA Pattern",
  e."aCL IgA" AS "aCL IgA",
  e.Diagnosis AS Examination_Diagnosis,
  e.Thrombosis AS Thrombosis,
  l.GOT AS GOT,
  l.GPT AS GPT,
  l.CRP AS CRP,
  l.WBC AS WBC,
  l.PLT AS PLT
FROM
  Examination e
  JOIN Laboratory l ON e.ID = l.ID AND e."Examination Date" = l.Date
accepted.description: Candidate pairs of Examination and Laboratory events that occur on the same date for the same patient. One row per matching event-pair, preserving both event dates and key measures to enable same-day comparisons. | Use for: Compare lab values on the same day as an examination; Assess whether thrombosis or antibody patterns align with abnormal labs on the same date

accepted.name: lab_running_avg_crp_window
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  Date,
  CRP,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ID ORDER BY Date) AS row_index,
  AVG(CRP) OVER (PARTITION BY ID ORDER BY Date ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS crp_rolling_avg_3
FROM
  Laboratory
accepted.description: Laboratory events with a 3-measure rolling average of CRP per patient ordered by Date. Exposes crp_rolling_avg_3 and row_index per patient to support moving-average trend analyses. Window size expressed as number of rows (3 most recent including current). | Use for: Identify trends or smoothing of CRP over recent visits; Detect sustained CRP elevation using moving average thresholds

accepted.name: ana_pattern_flags
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  "Examination Date",
  "ANA Pattern",
  CASE WHEN "ANA Pattern" LIKE '%P%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS ANA_P_flag,
  CASE WHEN "ANA Pattern" LIKE '%S%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS ANA_S_flag,
  CASE WHEN "ANA Pattern" LIKE '%N%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS ANA_N_flag
FROM
  Examination
accepted.description: Normalized boolean flags derived from the ANA Pattern textual field in Examination. Produces one row per examination event with indicator columns for common pattern tokens. Useful to filter or aggregate by presence of specific ANA pattern codes. This projection tokenizes by comma and marks presence; it does not assume a finite set (adds three common ones). | Use for: Filter examinations by presence of specific ANA pattern tokens; Aggregate counts of pattern types across patients or time

accepted.name: patients_with_exam_and_lab_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.ID,
  COALESCE(e.total_exams,0) AS total_exams,
  COALESCE(l.total_labs,0) AS total_labs,
  e.last_exam_date,
  l.last_lab_date
FROM
  (SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS total_exams, MAX("Examination Date") AS last_exam_date FROM Examination GROUP BY ID) e
  FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS total_labs, MAX(Date) AS last_lab_date FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID) l ON e.ID = l.ID
  RIGHT JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = COALESCE(e.ID, l.ID)
accepted.description: Per-patient counts of laboratory and examination events and the dates of most recent events. Useful for assessing data density per patient and for cohort inclusion based on available data. | Use for: Identify patients lacking lab or exam data; Select patients with at least N labs or exams (downstream WHERE)
